assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and credit cycles are a foundational mechanism in modern macro-finance. The Kiyotaki-Moore amplification and the financial accelerator shaped academic work and the policy analysis of the 2008 crisis. The work is rigorous dynamic general-equilibrium theory with wide reuse.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore wrote the core credit-cycle model. Gertler is the strongest complement through the financial accelerator and its quantitative macro development. Bernanke's 2022 prize overlaps with the accelerator literature, so the proposal centres on Kiyotaki-Moore and adds Gertler. Gilchrist is a plausible but more secondary fourth name.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from the 1990s and have had decades of confirmation and teaching use. The crisis gave an empirical test and stimulated extensions.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on financial crises may make the committee reluctant.
Gertler's credit is split across this ballot and the New Keynesian ballot.
Empirical identification of collateral channels is more mixed than the theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection reshaped trade theory and empirics. They changed how gains from trade are understood, through reallocation across firms and the extensive margin. The 2003 Melitz model is a workhorse across trade, macro and development, with strong policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the clear originator of the heterogeneous-firm model. Helpman has a broad record in new trade theory and in firm-level and exporter-versus-FDI work. Redding has important quantitative and spatial contributions, but they are a generation later and less central to the discovery. Krugman's 2008 prize covered earlier new trade theory.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of replication, extension and micro-data testing. The framework is standard in graduate teaching.
uncertainties: Attribution could also include Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not on this ballot.
Helpman's credit is split between this ballot and the trade-politics ballot.
The size of the welfare gains from selection is debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underlies modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. Interest-rate rules, the microfounded Phillips curve and welfare-based policy evaluation are of very high policy impact.
assessment.attribution: Credit is diffuse. Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (rules and staggered contracts), Woodford (the synthesis and normative analysis) and Galí (the empirical and theoretical NK model) are central. Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans (not on this ballot) and Smets, Wouters and Gertler are associated with the medium-scale DSGE implementation. Three is a hard constraint on a field with at least six strong claimants.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of use, though the 2008 crisis and later inflation episodes tested it.
uncertainties: The three-name limit forces an arbitrary cut among Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Galí and the DSGE group.
Past Nobel recognition of related macro work (Lucas, Prescott, Sargent, Sims, Bernanke) may reduce the marginal case.
Open debate over the empirical adequacy of the baseline NK model.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political economics systematically analyses how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and growth. It joins formal theory to cross-country and micro evidence. It is a substantial, coherent programme that opened a field.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini built the constitutional-design and electoral-rule programme. Besley's work on state capacity, accountability and political agency is closely connected. The 2024 prize for institutions and prosperity (Acemoglu, Johnson and Robinson) overlaps in theme but differs in mechanism and method.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of work, with major syntheses and a large empirical literature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize may reduce the marginal case.
Causal identification of constitutional effects is hard, and the evidence is contested.
Persson sits close to the Swedish economics community, but this is a disclosed proximity only.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law-and-finance programme made investor protection and legal institutions central to financial development. It is among the most cited bodies of work in finance and political economy, and it influenced reform debates.
assessment.attribution: The core is the La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny papers. The proposal keeps the three most consistently credited authors. Vishny has a strong claim as a coauthor and on separate corporate-finance work, but three names are allowed.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with 25+ years of citations. The legal-origins thesis has been heavily critiqued and revised.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques, including measurement of legal rules, endogeneity of legal origin and replication concerns, weigh on the case.
Reputational and conduct controversies around individual authors could affect committee views.
Whether the mechanism is law or broader institutions and history remains unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural estimation of demand and dynamic industry models changed empirical industrial organization and antitrust practice. The BLP random-coefficients demand estimator and dynamic-game estimation are workhorse tools across fields.
assessment.attribution: Pakes is the clearest central figure, with the BLP estimator, the Ericson-Pakes framework and the estimation methods. Berry and Levinsohn co-developed the estimator. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are also relevant and make a seven-name credit list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. The tools have been used for 30 years in merger review and academic work.
uncertainties: Credit is spread widely, and the trio may omit Bresnahan or others who made foundational contributions.
The credibility of structural assumptions is debated against reduced-form work.
The tools are an applied method rather than a single new conceptual discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based framework for technology and the China-shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers think about labour demand, polarization and the distributional costs of trade. The policy influence is large.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure across the task-based and trade-shock strands. Katz has a long record on skill-biased demand, with Goldin (2023 laureate) on education and technology. Hanson, with Autor and Dorn, anchors the trade-shock strand. Acemoglu, who is already a laureate, shaped the task framework, which complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature but still evolving. The China-shock results have been tested, extended and partly qualified.
uncertainties: Interaction with the 2024 prize and Goldin's 2023 prize, which both touch related themes.
The trade-shock estimates and their interpretation remain debated.
Possible tension between credit for conceptual versus empirical contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The top-income and wealth-distribution programme rebuilt long-run inequality measurement from tax data and moved inequality to the centre of economics and public debate. The data infrastructure, such as the World Inequality Database, is a lasting public good.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the original architects of the top-incomes series. Zucman extended the work to wealth and offshore holdings. Atkinson, who is deceased, contributed to the early programme and cannot be credited. Saez also appears on the optimal-taxation ballot.
assessment.maturity: Well established on measurement. Theory and policy implications, such as r > g and wealth taxes, are more contested and less settled.
uncertainties: Debate over methodology, such as the treatment of transfers, taxes and underreporting, affects reliability of the series.
The case rests more on measurement and data than on identified causal mechanisms.
The wealth-tax policy advocacy may make some committee members cautious.
